ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure is a buck chopper circuit, with the DC power supply on the left labeled 100 V; after the switch, there is a freewheeling diode branch; on the load side, the series inductor is labeled 200 mH, the resistive load is labeled 5 Ω, and the direction of load current i is drawn in the right-side loop. Reasoning: The problem gives the switching frequency f = 1 kHz and duty cycle D = 0.5. Therefore, the period T = 1/f = 1 ms, and the on-time Ton = DT = 0.5 ms. The average output voltage of the buck chopper Vout,avg = DVs = 0.5 × 100 = 50 V. The average load current is approximately Iavg = 50/5 = 10 A. During conduction, the inductor voltage is approximately VL = Vs − R Iavg = 100 − 5×10 = 50 V. The increase in inductor current is ΔI = (VL/L) Ton = (50/0.2) × 0.0005 = 0.125 A. This increase is the peak-to-peak ripple of the steady-state triangular-wave current, so the peak-to-peak ripple of the load current is approximately 0.125 A.

raw_record.question_text: The figure shows a step-down chopper switched at 1 kHz with a duty ratio \(D = 0.5\). What is the approximate peak-to-peak ripple in the load current?

method.method_draft: From the image, take Vs = 100 V, L = 200 mH = 0.2 H, and R = 5 Ω. From the text, take f = 1 kHz and D = 0.5, so T = 1 ms and Ton = 0.5 ms. For a step-down chopper, Vout,avg = DVs = 50 V, so Iavg = 50/5 = 10 A. During the on interval, the inductor voltage is approximately 100 − 5(10) = 50 V, so the current rises by ΔI = (50/0.2)(0.0005) = 0.125 A. This rise equals the peak-to-peak ripple, so report about 0.125 A.

method.method_draft: From the text, use f = 1 kHz and D = 0.5, so Ton = Toff = 0.0005 s. From the image, use R = 5 Ω and L = 0.2 H, giving τ = L/R = 0.04 s and a = exp(−0.0005/0.04). method.CoT_raw:
Image description: The attached circuit diagram shows a step-down chopper supplied by a 100 V DC source. The load path includes an inductor labeled 200 mH in series with a resistor labeled 5 Ω, and a freewheeling diode is connected for the off interval.

Reasoning: The switching frequency is f = 1 kHz, so the period is T = 1/f = 0.001 s. With duty ratio D = 0.5, Ton = 0.0005 s and Toff = 0.0005 s. From the image, R = 5 Ω and L = 0.2 H, so the load time constant is τ = L/R = 0.2/5 = 0.04 s. The exponential factor for each half-cycle is a = exp(-0.0005/0.04) ≈ exp(-0.0125) ≈ 0.9876.

Let Imin be the current at the start of on-time and Imax at the end of on-time. During on-time, the RL current tends toward 100/5 = 20 A, so Imax = 20 + (Imin - 20)a. During off-time, the current decays through the freewheeling path, so Imin = a Imax. Solving these periodic equations gives the ripple: Imax - Imin = 20(1 - a)/(1 + a). Substituting a ≈ 0.9876 gives ΔI ≈ 20(0.0124)/(1.9876) ≈ 0.125 A peak-to-peak.
